paths.description: Homepage/listing template and primary discovery surface; desktop, 360px, preference, performance, network, accessibility, privacy and memory conditions. Represents the general movie-grid template.
Telugu 2026 category listing, selected as the section/index archetype. Other language/year categories share this template and were not duplicated.
Vadala movie detail, selected as the content/entity archetype. Other movie records share this template and were not duplicated.
Primary search journey with query “Vadala”; request reached a Cloudflare verification interstitial instead of results.
Invalid-route recovery state, selected to test HTTP failure messaging and navigation recovery.

artifacts.condition: prefers-color-scheme: dark; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; prefers-contrast: more

artifacts.condition: prefers-color-scheme: dark; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; prefers-contrast: more

findings.summary: The theme is hard-coded dark rather than following the user color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode probe matched prefers-color-scheme: dark but found color-scheme: normal and no preference media rules; the dark screenshot is pixel-identical in size to the default capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules, and the representative listing and detail pages use ordinary cross-document navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-aware navigation chrome or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 7,383 CSS px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or scroll-aware sticky treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or lightweight progress/affordance treatment for the long listing.

findings.summary: Navigation does not visibly cue the destination or current context.
findings.evidence: Home, category, and detail screenshots show the same nav treatment without a clear current-section marker, transition, or post-navigation highlight.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the current section with aria-current and visible styling; use directional transitions or highlights where they clarify movement.

findings.summary: An injected full-viewport advertisement intercepts the page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found body.home > a#dontfoid as a fixed 412x823 link covering the viewport, inserted by advertising code, with no accessible name or dismiss control.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the click-intercepting ad integration. If promotion is necessary, keep it visibly bounded, labelled, non-modal, and dismissible.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is tied only to viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container or container-type use; reused movie cards and side content depend on global media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/list regions containment and adapt them with size container queries while retaining a fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is removed from links and several controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reported outline: none and no box shadow for navigation and movie links. Search controls are 26px high and nav items are 40px high, below a robust 44px touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a clear high-contrast outline and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: The primary search journey is blocked by bot verification.
findings.evidence: Submitting a representative search produced a Cloudflare “Performing security verification” page instead of results, with no usable search result or alternate completion path.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot protection so ordinary search GET requests complete, preserve the query through challenges, and provide a recoverable fallback.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts ship substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 94 KiB of unused JavaScript: 68,935 bytes in Google Tag Manager and 27,206 bytes in aclib.js. HAR shows scripts transfer 233,845 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the ad script where possible, reduce analytics tags, and conditionally load non-essential third-party code after user intent.

findings.summary: A viewport-covering link has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse link-name failed on body.home > a#dontfoid, a fixed full-screen anchor in the tab order without text, aria-label, or title.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the injected overlay. Every remaining interactive element must have a meaningful accessible name and purpose.

findings.summary: Focus indication and list semantics are broken.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline: none on links. Lighthouse also reported sidebar li elements whose parent no longer exposes list semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible :focus-visible styles and keep list items in semantic list containers without overriding their list role.

findings.summary: Touch targets are too small despite successful narrow-screen reflow.
findings.evidence: At the tested layout, search controls were 26px high and top navigation links 40px high; mobile layout otherwise had zero horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control hit areas to roughly 44px, preserve the valid viewport meta, and recheck at narrow/zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: Movie posters are distorted and low-resolution at rendered size.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported poster images displayed at a 0.88 ratio from 0.75 source assets and flagged low-resolution examples; CSS forces poster height to 200px.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratio with height:auto or aspect-ratio and provide correctly sized responsive image variants.

findings.summary: The public site has no usable sitemap.
findings.evidence: robots.txt returns 200 but is empty, while /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 404. Canonical URLs otherwise point to the final .vote host.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap on the canonical host and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Movie entities lack structured data.
findings.evidence: The home and representative detail DOM contained Open Graph metadata but no application/ld+json; movie detail content is eligible for schema.org Movie metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for WebSite/SearchAction and Movie entities, matching visible titles, images, cast, and synopsis.

findings.summary: Core security headers are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but no Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. X-Frame-Options was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy; validate third-party requirements before rollout.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising requests are disproportionate and opaque.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found seven third-party origins, including Google Analytics, adexchangerapid.com and usrpubtrk.com. HAR recorded 13 third-party requests and 234,572 transferred bytes, including eight analytics calls.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the advertising tracker chain, consolidate analytics to one data-minimised configuration, and load optional tracking only after appropriate consent.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP/frame-ancestors policy, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; only X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add modern browser policies, preferring CSP frame-ancestors alongside a nonce/hash-based script policy, plus HSTS and restrictive referrer/permissions policies.

findings.summary: Navigation submenus depend on hover and manual absolute positioning.
findings.evidence: CSS shows nested menus hidden with display:none and revealed only by li:hover, positioned with fixed top/left offsets; no focus-within, popover, or anchor-position fallback is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Make submenu disclosure keyboard/touch operable and use semantic controls with resilient positioning/fallbacks near viewport edges.

findings.summary: The multilingual catalogue is not layout-ready for other writing directions.
findings.evidence: html lang="en-US" is present, but CSS inspection found no logical properties and 40 physical left/right declarations across a site organised around multiple language catalogues.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties, retain correct per-page lang, and add dir support before localising UI or titles.

findings.summary: The full-page ad overlay is a disguised, unlabeled action.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a fixed, viewport-sized outbound affiliate anchor (#dontfoid) with no visible or accessible label, so an ordinary click can become an unexpected ad navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove click hijacking and make every commercial action visible, labelled, proportionate, and user initiated.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not responsive or modern.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 32/32 legacy JPGs, 32/32 without srcset, and 28 below-fold images without lazy loading. Lighthouse also found distorted/low-resolution posters.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, add srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold posters, and preserve source aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Background analytics and ad work is wasteful.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded eight analytics calls plus ad/tracking requests; 94 KiB of third-party JavaScript was estimated unused, despite the page’s simple server-rendered directory function.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate redundant tags and ad calls, batch necessary telemetry, and defer low-value work until after user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes too much of the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 234,572 of 593,649 bytes (39.5%); GTM alone transferred 165,947 bytes and ad scripts added 66,890 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove the ad chain, reduce tag-manager payload, and cache/defer only integrations with clear user value.

taskList.title: Remove the full-viewport click-hijacking ad overlay
Restore visible focus and robust touch targets
Unblock ordinary search requests from bot verification
Remove or minimise ad and analytics third parties
Make navigation resilient, contextual, and keyboard/touch operable
Add structured metadata and a valid sitemap
Adopt component queries, logical properties, and route transitions
